doc.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Ed Thigpen, Jimmy Cobb and Grady Tate
summary: Short remarks on Thigpen's rim shot and Grady Tate telling him to play his chrome sandwich.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Oh, absolutely. [laughs] Going through your discography, I saw…
Oh, he passed away in Denmark, right? I played once in a while with him. He was so great for that rim shot on the fourth beat. One, two, three, pop.
That’s Philly Joe. He actually… Jimmy Cobb?
[inaudible] he did it [inaudible], it’s history with him and Miles. They’re [walking?] [inaudible].
Now when I went through your discography, I saw you did a lot of work with Grady Tate.
‘Cause he maybe he’s a studio drummer so he’s doing a lot of work.

No, he was… He was… on some of the dates with Quincy, he played the drums. And when, with Peggy Lee. And when I talked too much, he said, “Hey, Tits, shut up and play your chrome sandwich.” That’s Grady. [laughs] See, you wanted anecdotes. You got it. “Hey, Tits. Shut up, man, and play your chrome sandwich.” So that’s Grady. That’s Grady. [laughs] I hope he’s okay, because he must be up in, in those numbers. Not far from mine. [laughs]
